main_body: Repeating stone-brick wall/paving pattern filling the whole tile area; flat terrain texture, not a standing object
top_band: none: the terrain tile has no top/front split. The column scan shows a repeating brick course: 1px light edge L176, 5px face L143, then 2px dark mortar shadow L115 and L90
evidence: The kind is terrain (wall face or paving autotile), so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. It is a tiling brick surface with no standing volume and no receding side faces. Each brick has a light top edge, a mid face and a dark mortar shadow underneath, which reads correctly as a wall or floor texture. Passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The piece has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile. The paving reference has 7 and 7, and the grass reference has 80 and 26. Dark mortar and edge pixels are 100% near-neutral (#4b4245, #625756), so the outline reads as a grey/black sticker line rather than a tint of the adjacent material. The brick faces are mostly one flat tone (L143) with only a few sparse speckle dots, and the courses repeat identically with no per-brick shading. 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0% only because of those dots. It is thinner and more mechanical than the references, so it fails.
